e-8592.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
e-8592.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) =  \langle 1, \, \sqrt{2} t,\, -t^2 \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
e-8592.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨1,\,\sqrt{2}t,\,-{t}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩ \\  & =2t+2{t}^{3} \\  & =2t({t}^{2}+1), \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}t)}^{2}+{(-{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}} \\  & ={t}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2t({t}^{2}+1)}{{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{-2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives v(t)=⟨2,3t²,2t⟩ and a(t)=⟨0,6t,2⟩. Thus v·a=18t³+4t and ||v||=√(4+9t⁴+4t²). The tangential component a_T=(v·a)/||v|| matches option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩ \\  & =18{t}^{3}+4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{18{t}^{3}+4t}{\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨2t,t3,t2⟩. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
 6t+42+9t4+4t2
b
 18t2+44+3t2+2t
c
 18t3+4t4+9t4+4t2
d
6t32+3t2+2t2
e
 3t24+6t4+2t2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(t3),ddt(t2)⟩=⟨2,3t2,2t⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(2),ddt(3t2),ddt(2t)⟩=⟨0,6t,2⟩.

Then, we compute v⋅a and ||v||:

v⋅a=⟨2,3t2,2t⟩⋅⟨0,6t,2⟩=18t3+4t||v||=22+(3t2)2+(2t)2=4+9t4+4t2

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=18t3+4t4+9t4+4t2.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution declares option c, agreeing with the independent calculation: v=⟨2,3t²,2t⟩, a=⟨0,6t,2⟩, and a_T=(v·a)/||v||=(18t³+4t)/√(4+9t⁴+4t²). The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option e.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩ \\  & =18{t}^{3}+4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{18{t}^{3}+4t}{\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨tet,−et,4⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
te2t(t2+1)e2t+16
b
(t2+1)e2te2t+16
c
(t+1)e2tt2+16
d
e2tt2+16
e
(t2+t+1)e2t(t2+1)e2t+16
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives a(t)=⟨(t+1)e^t,−e^t,0⟩. Hence v·a=(t²+t+1)e^{2t} and ||v||=√((t²+1)e^{2t}+16). Therefore a_T=(v·a)/||v|| is option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩\cdot ⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =t(t+1){e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+0, \\  & =({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+16} \\  & =\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: a=⟨ddt(tet),ddt(−et),ddt(4)⟩=⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩

Next, we compute v⋅a and ||v||: v⋅a=⟨tet,−et,4⟩⋅⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩=t(t+1)e2t+e2t+0,=(t2+t+1)e2t,||v||=(tet)2+(−et)2+(4)2=t2e2t+e2t+16=(t2+1)e2t+16

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=(t2+t+1)e2t(t2+1)e2t+16.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩\cdot ⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =t(t+1){e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+0, \\  & =({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+16} \\  & =\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}}.\end{aligned}
$$
